business_problem: The process began with exploratory sessions, including regular scoping and envisioning meetings. Liam Donohoe, Principal Architect, Data & Analytics Platforms at bp, presented his team’s work on the modular reuse of data products to create an ecosystem of data across the company’s federated data platform environments. That’s what brought home the potential power of a data mesh implementation at bp,” says Donohoe.
solution_summary: BP built this solution on Azure Data Factory, Azure Databricks, Azure Synapse Analytics, Power BI. The process began with exploratory sessions, including regular scoping and envisioning meetings. Azure Data Factory moves and orchestrates data from source systems into the analytics platform. Azure Databricks processes, transforms, and engineers large data sets for analytics and machine learning. Azure Synapse Analytics models and analyzes enterprise data for reporting, AI, and decision support. Power BI publishes dashboards and self-service analytics to business users. bp reached out to Microsoft, already its long-time cloud provider, for insights into how it might adapt its data lakes to a more modern, distributed architecture. Both companies dedicated teams to the creation of the solution, which would take shape as a modular data mesh based on the Microsoft Intelligent Data Platform and incorporate Azure Databricks Azure Synapse Analytics Micr.

data_flow: Operational data is ingested through Azure Data Factory from line-of-business systems, engineered and transformed in Azure Databricks before Power BI dashboards surface insights to business users.
business_outcome: A major benefit of bp’s data platform is its modularity. Each new digital service the company creates is designed to consolidate the activities, technologies, services, and resources required to deliver a specific business outcome, and can also be used over and over by many different teams in service of multiple products while preserving data ownership at its point of origin.
